```{python}
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Markdown, HTML, display

import helpers as h
from helpers import colour_bar_figure, colour_current_series, num, pct, show, status_badge

d = h.load()
st = h.status(d)
above = st[st.level.isin(["high", "elevated"])]
record = st[st.level == "high"]
if h.selection_note():
    display(Markdown(h.selection_note()))
```

## Situation at a glance

```{python}
normal_or_low = len(st) - len(above)
summary_html = f"""
<div class="summary-grid">
  <div class="summary-card neutral">
    <div class="label">Surveillance indicators monitored</div>
    <div class="value">{len(st)}</div>
  </div>
  <div class="summary-card normal">
    <div class="label">Normal / low</div>
    <div class="value">{normal_or_low}</div>
  </div>
  <div class="summary-card elevated">
    <div class="label">Above normal</div>
    <div class="value">{len(st[st.level == 'elevated'])}</div>
  </div>
  <div class="summary-card high">
    <div class="label">Record high</div>
    <div class="value">{len(record)}</div>
  </div>
</div>
"""
display(HTML(summary_html))

def latest_data(st):
    """Latest period per reporting frequency; monthly series do not all end in the same month."""
    weekly = st[st.frequency.isin(["iso_week", "week"])]
    # A report can cover a subset of diseases, so any frequency may be absent.
    parts = []
    if len(weekly):
        parts.append(f"{weekly.period_label.iloc[weekly.period.argmax()]} for the {len(weekly)} weekly series")
    monthly = st[st.frequency == "month"]
    for period, rows in sorted(monthly.groupby("period"), reverse=True):
        parts.append(f"{rows.period_label.iloc[0]} for {len(rows)} monthly series ({', '.join(rows.disease)})")
    for row in st[st.frequency == "year"].itertuples():
        parts.append(f"{row.period_label} for {row.disease} (yearly)")
    return "; ".join(parts)


names = ", ".join(record.disease)
record_text = f" Record-high indicators: **{names}**." if len(record) else ""
display(Markdown(
    f"**{len(above)} of {len(st)}** monitored surveillance indicators are above their usual level for the time of year."
    f"{record_text}\n\n"
    f"Each indicator is compared with its comparison window: the same week or month in previous years. "
    f"Latest data: {latest_data(st)}."))
```

```{python}
table = pd.DataFrame({
    "Indicator": st.disease,
    "Level": st.level_label,
    "Latest": st.value.map(num),
    "Period": st.period_label,
    "Usual (median)": st["median"].map(num),
    "Compared with usual": st.ratio.map(h.versus_usual),
})
show(table, levels=st.level)
```

**Colour guide:** <span class="status-badge status-high">Record high</span> latest value is the highest for this period in the comparison window. <span class="status-badge status-elevated">Above normal</span> at least 20% and at least 3 cases above the comparison-window median. <span class="status-badge status-normal">Normal / low</span> not currently above the usual level.

## Indicators above the usual level

The **coloured line** is the reported series: **red** for record-high status and **yellow** for above-normal status. The dashed blue line is the median and the grey band the minimum to maximum of the **comparison window**: the same week or month in previous years (5 or 10 years; FOPH's own windows also include the current value).

```{python}
for row in above.itertuples():
    s = h.series(d, row.topic)
    unit = "cases were reported" if row.measure == "cases" else "GP consultations are estimated"
    ytd = (f" Calendar year to date: {num(row.ytd)} ({pct(row.ytd_pct)} on the same period last year)."
           if not pd.isna(row.ytd_pct) else "")
    small = " Counts are small, so the level can change on a few cases." if row.value < 60 else ""
    badge = status_badge(row.level, row.level_label)
    display(Markdown(
        f"### {row.disease} {badge}\n\n"
        f"**{num(row.value)}** {unit} in {row.period_label}, {h.versus_usual(row.ratio)} for this time of year "
        f"(median {num(row.median)}, range {num(row.min)} to {num(row.max)}).{ytd}{small}"))
    fig = h.trend_figure(s)
    colour_current_series(fig, row.level).show()
```

## Where: cantons with the highest incidence

Cases per 100,000 residents. Cantons with fewer than 5 cases are left out because their rates are unstable. Canton figures are published for the last full year for most infections, and weekly for influenza and COVID-19.

### Map by canton

Choose a disease from the menu above the map. Each canton is coloured by its cases per 100,000 residents, from yellow (lowest) through green and teal to dark purple (highest). Grey cantons had fewer than 5 cases. Hover over a canton for its figures. The data are published by canton, not by city.

```{python}
h.canton_map(d, ramp=h.MAP_RAMP_MULTI).show()
```

### Cantons with the highest incidence, for indicators above the usual level

```{python}
shown = 0
for row in above.itertuples():
    regions, when = h.regional(d, row.topic)
    regions = regions[regions.cases >= 5].head(10) if len(regions) else regions
    if len(regions) < 3:
        continue
    shown += 1
    fig = h.bar_figure(regions, "incidence", "canton", f"{row.disease}: top cantons, {when}",
                       "Cases per 100,000")
    colour_bar_figure(fig, row.level).show()
if not shown:
    display(Markdown("No canton-level data for the indicators currently above normal."))
```

## Burden this year compared with last year

Cumulative total from January to the latest period, against the same span one year earlier.

```{python}
ytd = st.dropna(subset=["ytd_pct"]).sort_values("ytd_pct", ascending=False)
show(pd.DataFrame({
    "Indicator": ytd.disease,
    "Category": ytd.group,
    "Calendar year to date": ytd.ytd.map(num),
    "Same period last year": ytd.ytd_prev.map(num),
    "Change": ytd.ytd_pct.map(pct),
    "Data up to": ytd.period_label,
}))
```

## Respiratory season watch

Weekly respiratory indicators at the start of the season. The recent change compares the last 4 weeks with the 4 weeks before.

```{python}
resp = st[st.group == "Respiratory"]
show(pd.DataFrame({
    "Indicator": resp.disease,
    "Level": resp.level_label,
    "Latest week": resp.value.map(num),
    "Per 100,000": resp.incidence.map(lambda x: num(x, 1)),
    "Change, last 4 weeks": resp.change_pct.map(pct),
}), levels=resp.level)
```

```{python}
for topic in resp.topic:
    if topic not in set(above.topic):
        r = resp[resp.topic == topic].iloc[0]
        fig = h.trend_figure(h.series(d, topic), height=260)
        colour_current_series(fig, r.level).show()
```

## How to read this report

- **Source.** Federal Office of Public Health (FOPH) surveillance data, cleaned and merged by the project pipeline into `results/harmonised.csv`.
- **Colour coding.** Red indicates the report's existing `high` / record-high category, yellow the existing `elevated` / above-normal category, and green normal or low categories. The colours are visual cues; they do not introduce a new clinical risk classification.
- **Reported cases are not all infections.** They depend on who gets tested and reported. COVID-19 case counts in particular under-estimate infections.
- **GP figures are estimates** extrapolated from the Sentinella network of practices.
- **Comparison window.** The same week or month in previous years: FOPH's published 5- or 10-year minimum, median and maximum where available (these include the current value), otherwise the previous 5 years of the series. "Usual" in this report means the median of that window.
- **The COVID-19 comparison window includes pandemic years**, so "low" there is relative to an exceptional period.
- **Sexually transmitted infections lag by several months** in publication.
- **No statistical testing is applied.** Levels are descriptive comparisons with the comparison window.
